name: birch tree

attributes.attribute: holds the second slot of the Tree Alphabet
a short-lived but graceful tree with white bark
wood for the Maypole used in Beltane dances
the feast that uses the Maypole in dance

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text:
The birch is one of the sacred plants of the Celts. Its sign holds the second slot of the Tree Alphabet. The birch species betula is short-lived. Still it is graceful, with pale white bark.

The wood of the birch gives a pole to hold. The Celts shaped it into a Maypole for the dances. Those dances came at the feast of Beltane. So the birch holds its place in the rites of the old Celts.

okr.objective: Cite the birch as a sacred tree and the second letter of the Tree Alphabet.
key_results: The birch takes the second slot in the Tree Alphabet.
Its bark is white, and it is graceful despite a short life.
Birch wood formed the Maypole used in Beltane dances.
